'''Marilyn Levy''' (April 3, 1922 – June 19, 2014) was an American chemist and inventor based at [[Fort Monmouth]]. She was awarded the [[United States Army]]'s [[Department of the Army Meritorious Civilian Service Award|Meritorious Civilian Service Award]] in 1971.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|date=1971-06-13|title=Army Awards Miss Levy Meritorious Civilian Medal|pages=70|work=Asbury Park Press|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84060142/army-awards-miss-levy-meritorious/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Marilyn Levy was born in [[New York City]], the daughter of Moses (Morris) Levy and Rachel (Rae) Levy. Both of her parents were Jewish and also born in New York. She attended [[Hunter College High School]] and [[Hunter College]], completing a bachelor's degree in chemistry in 1942.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://www.monmouthcountyclerk.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/2017-Catalog-Inventors-Final-v2.pdf|title=New Jersey in Focus: Inventors and Innovators in Monmouth County|publisher=Monmouth County Archives|date=October 2017|pages=94–95}}</ref> She pursued graduate studies in chemistry at the [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering|Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|date=July 1975|title=ECOM's 'First Lady' GS-15; Marilyn Levy Climaxes Research Career|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xt8fw8GQj4UC&dq=%22Marilyn%20Levy%22%20Hunter%20College&pg=RA1-PA24|journal=Army Research and Development News Magazine|volume=16|pages=24}}</ref>

== Career ==
Beginning in 1953,<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|date=1971-06-29|title=High Honor Goes to Miss Levy|pages=8|work=The Daily Register|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84058257/high-honor-goes-to-miss-levy/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Levy worked as a chemist at Fort Monmouth,<ref>{{Cite journal|date=October 1962|title=Four of Fort Monmouth's Many Inventors|url=https://archive.org/details/sim_civil-service-journal_october-december-1962_3_2/page/26/mode/2up|journal=Civil Service Journal|volume=3|pages=26|via=Internet Archive}}</ref> where she "received international acclaim as a pioneer and as an expert in photographic research".<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|date=September 1972|title=Women in Army Science... Women's Lib in Army Labs Long Predates Modern Movement|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-SQ_MX2DZ-gC&dq=Marilyn+Levy+Army&pg=RA5-PA38|journal=Army Research and Development News Magazine|volume=13|pages=38}}</ref> She held more than twenty patents on film developing processes.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite news|date=1979-05-20|title=Fort Employees Get 2 Patents for Photography Development|pages=43|work=Asbury Park Press|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84059992/fort-employees-get-2-patents-for/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Beardsley|first=Frank|date=1972-06-18|title=Woman Speeds Color Print Processing|pages=48|work=Asbury Park Press|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84060343/woman-speeds-color-print/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She was head of the Photo Optics Technical Area (POTA), Combat Surveillance and Target Acquisition Laboratory, and the first woman in the United States Army Electronics Command (ECOM) to reach grade GS-15.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|date=1975-06-25|title=Chemist Earns GS-15|pages=60|work=Asbury Park Press|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84059004/chemist-earns-gs-15/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She retired in 1979.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1979-09-27|title=Retired Scientist is Honored|pages=23|work=The Daily Register|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84058823/retired-scientist-is-honored/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

In 1971, Levy received the Army's Meritorious Civilian Service Award.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":2" /> In 1973, she received the Army Research and Development Achievement Award.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1973-11-13|title=Three ECOM Employes Get Army Achievement Awards|pages=12|work=The Daily Register|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84059172/three-ecom-employes-get-army/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She was nominated twice for the [[Federal Woman's Award]], but did not receive that honor. She was a member of the [[Royal Photographic Society]], the [[American Chemical Society]],<ref>{{Cite news|last=Benjock|first=Mary Lou|date=1965-10-24|title=Women Rank High at Army Command|pages=17|work=Asbury Park Press|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/84058613/women-rank-high-at-army-commandmary/|access-date=2021-08-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and [[Society for Imaging Science and Technology|Society of Photographic Scientists and Engineers]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|date=April 1967|title=Names in the News|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HFQbAQAAMAAJ&dq=%22Marilyn+Levy%22+Fort+Monmouth&pg=RA7-PA78|journal=Signals|volume=21|pages=78}}</ref> She served on the editorial board of the ''Journal of Applied Photographic Engineering'' and ''Photographic Science and Engineering''.<ref name=":1" />

== Patents ==
Marilyn Levy patented several photographic processes, methods, and materials during her work for the American military, including:

* ''Photothermographic substance'' (1956), with Heinz Schulze<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Photothermographic substance|gdate=1955-03-08|country=US|number=2758028|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn|inventor2-last=Schulze|inventor2-first=Heinz}}</ref>
* ''Sensitizer for photothermographic substances'' (1956)<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Sensitizer for photothermographic substances|gdate=1954-07-28|country=US|number=2756146|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn}}</ref>
* ''Monobaths containing sodium polyacrylate and polyvinyl-pyrrolidone'' (1965)<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Monobaths containing sodium polyacrylate and polyvinyl-pyrrolidone|gdate=1961-05-26|country=US|number=3167429|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn}}</ref>
* ''Viscous processing solution'' (1966)<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Viscous processing solution|gdate=1966-03-01|country=US|number=3238043|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn}}</ref>
* ''Photographic processing apparatus'' (1966), with Seymour L. Hersh<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Photographic processing apparatus|fdate=1964-05-05|country=US|number=3264970
|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor2-last=Levy|inventor2-first=Marilyn|inventor1-last=Hersh|inventor1-first=Seymour L.}}</ref>
* ''Image forming material and method of forming an image therefrom'' (1971)<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Image forming material and method of forming an image therefrom|gdate=1969-11-02|country=US|number=3600170|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn}}</ref>
* ''Color printing method'' (1972)<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Color printing method|gdate=1971-04-15|country=US|number=3672766|assign=[[Secretary of the Navy]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn}}</ref>
* ''Curve analysis method in color photography'' (1976)<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Curve analysis method in color photography|gdate=1975-03-04|country=US|number=3953135|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn|inventor2-last=Schwartz|inventor2-first=Milan}}</ref>
* ''Filter pack correction method in color photography'' (1979), with Milan Schwartz<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Filter pack correction method in color photography|fdate=1975-03-04|country=US
|number=4146394|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn|inventor2-last=Schwartz|inventor2-first=Milan}}</ref>
* ''Reconnaissance/surveillance system utilizing color signature of target'' (granted 1979), with Vincent W. Ball<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Reconnaissance/surveillance system utilizing color signature of target|country=US|number=4143971|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn|inventor2-last=Ball|inventor2-first=Vincent W.|pubdate=1979-03-13}}</ref>
* ''Method and apparatus for manufacturing masked motion picture film for simulated target practice'' (1981), with Seymour L. Hersh<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Method and apparatus for manufacturing masked motion picture film for simulated target practice|gdate=1979-05-18||country=US|number=4264157|assign=[[Secretary of the Army]]|inventor1-last=Levy|inventor1-first=Marilyn|inventor2-last=Hersh|inventor2-first=Seymour L.}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
A longtime resident of [[Little Silver, New Jersey]], Levy died in 2014, aged 92 years, in [[Red Bank, New Jersey]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=July 4, 2014|title=In Memoriam: Marilyn Levy|page=9|work=The Two River Times|url=https://tworivertimes.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/09-OBITS.pdf|access-date=August 24, 2021}}</ref>
